name: Congenital Megacalycosis

criteria.description: Non-obstructive dilatation of the renal calyces without pelvis or ureteral dilatation
Normal renal pelvis size and morphology on imaging
No evidence of urinary tract obstruction clinically or radiologically
Unilateral or bilateral involvement of renal calyces
Preserved renal function without signs of renal impairment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of non-obstructive calyceal dilatation with normal renal pelvis and absence of obstruction on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological and requires exclusion of obstructive causes of calyceal dilatation.

laboratory: Urinalysis may show mild hematuria or proteinuria
imaging: Ultrasound showing dilated renal calyces with normal renal pelvis and ureters
Intravenous urography demonstrating non-obstructive calyceal enlargement
CT urography confirming absence of obstruction
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; considered sporadic or familial in rare cases
other: Differentiation from obstructive uropathies critical for management

distinguishingFeatures: Dilated renal pelvis and ureter involvement
Impaired renal function in advanced cases
Often associated with renal tubular acidosis
Different imaging pattern with cystic medullary dilatation

references: S. B. Smith et al., 'Congenital Megacalycosis: Clinical and Radiological Features,' Journal of Pediatric Urology, 2018
National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD) - Megacalycosis
